title: Design of novel gold nanocluster and its composites for cancer cell imaging and tumor bio-marking
protocol: Culture HepG2 cells in 7 × 9 culture flasks in 15 mL medium at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Incubate HepG2 cells of a whole culture flask with 10 μmol/L HAuCl4 solution for 24 or 48 h at 37 °C, 5% CO2.
Trypsinize the incubated HepG2 cells and harvest the cells in eppendorf tubes.
Disperse the cells in PBS, centrifuge the mixture at 1000 rpm for 5 min and collect the cells.
Repeat this procedure three times.
Re-disperse the collected cells in 2 mL Milli-Q water and use the cells for extracting the gold nanoclusters.
Extract the gold nanoclusters from incubated HepG2 cells by a frequently repetitive freeze-thaw method from -20 °C to 37 °C for ~5 h.
Centrifuge the mixture at 1500 rpm for 3 min.
Discard the precipitated cell debris and collect the supernatant with gold nanoclusters.
Dilute the above supernatant 5 times.
Add 2 mL of the above diluted mixture to a cuvette.
Record UV/Vis absorbance spectra (700-200 nm) for the obtained gold nanoclusters with scan speed 120 nm/min.
Dilute the supernatant 5 times.
Add 2 mL of the diluted mixture to a cuvette.
Place the cuvette at the sample cell position.
Record fluorescence spectra (500-700 nm) for the obtained gold nanoclusters with a scan speed of 60 nm/min at excitation wavelength 470 nm (Excitation Slit 3 nm; Emission Slit 3 nm).
Sonicate the supernatant for ~3 h.
Disperse 5 μL of the supernatant with decuple dilution on copper grids, and dry overnight.
Acquire the TEM image of gold nanoclusters.
Freeze-dry the supernatant overnight and collect the pale yellow powder.
Record X-ray photoelectron spectra of the gold nanoclusters from the mixture.
Set the typical operating pressure at around 5 × 10^-10 Torr in the analysis chamber.
Take survey spectra (0–1000 eV) at a constant analyzer pass energy of 160 eV.
Acquire high-resolution spectra for Au4f with a pass energy of 60 eV, a step of 0.1 eV and a dwell time of 1000 ms.
Fit the XPS peaks using XPSPEAK v. 4.1 software.
Use the Shirley function as a background for fitting.
Fit individual peaks by a Gaussian-Lorentzian cross-product.
Seed HepG2 cells on ITO glass substrate in DMEM with 10% FBS and 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37 °C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere overnight.
Add 2 μL of HAuCl4 stock solution to achieve a final concentration of 10 μmol/L.
Gently shake the dish to ensure good mixing.
Incubate the dish at 37 °C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere for 24 or 48 h.
Rinse the incubated cells three times with PBS.
Dehydrate through series of ethanol washes: 30%, 50%, 70%, 90%, 95%, and 100%.
Transfer to critical point drying apparatus containing ethanol as an intermediate reagent.
Use a suitable holding device for the transfer.
Seed HepG2, K562, or L02 cells on quartz substrate in cell culture dish containing DMEM with 10% (vol/vol) FBS and 1% (vol/vol) penicillin-streptomycin.
Incubate the seeded cells at 37 °C in a humidified 5% CO2 atmosphere overnight.
Prepare the fluorescence or Raman imaging sample by following Steps 24-26 of the PROCEDURE.
Place the prepared cell sample on CLSM objective stage for fluorescence imaging.
Record cell imaging for the incubated cells using confocal laser scanning microscopy with a 488-nm excitation laser beam focused using a 20 × IR coated objective.
Gently remove PBS and transfer the prepared cell sample to Raman microscope objective stage for Raman spectroscopy.
Record cell Raman spectroscopy by confocal Raman microscopy with an excitation wavelength at 532 nm.
Use 50% laser intensity for the recording.
Overlay the spectra twice with 100 s integration time.
Inject HAuCl4 solution prepared in PBS (100 μL of 10 mmol/L) into BALB/c mice bearing HepG2 or K562 tumors near the tumor location through subcutaneous injection.
Maintain injected mice in a specific pathogen-free house at 24 ± 2 °C with a standard 12-hour light/12-hour dark cycle for 24, 48, or 72 hours.
Anesthetize the experimental mouse with 5% isoflurane (21% oxygen, balance nitrogen) in an induction chamber until breathing is slow and deep at different time points post injection.
Position the mouse on its back on a microscope stage for imaging during the imaging procedures under isoflurane anesthesia.
Select the appropriate excitation wavelength (488 nm).
Adjust the mouse’s posture as needed while monitoring the live image.
Record in vivo images of the mice using Maestro EX in vivo fluorescence imaging system at different time points post injection.
Dissolve 1.0 g HAuCl4•4H2O in Millipore water to make 1% (w/v) HAuCl4•4H2O solution.
Load 169.2 g TOAB into 16 ml chloroform in a three-neck flask.
Add 6 ml of 1% (w/v) HAuCl4•4H2O solution to the flask and mix vigorously at room temperature until HAuCl4 is transferred to the organic phase.
Add 40.2 μL of 1-DT into the flask and stir for 10 minutes.
Prepare a fresh 1.55 mol/L NaBH4 solution.
Load 25 ml of 1.55 mol/L NaBH4 solution drop-wise into the flask, observing color change to deep purple within seconds.
Stir the bi-phase solution for 3 hours at room temperature.
Separate the organic phase with a separating funnel and load it into a new 50 ml flask.
Evaporate the separated organic solution using a rotary evaporator at 50°C for 4 minutes.
Re-dissolve the product in 2 mL chloroform.
Precipitate the product in 80 mL ethanol in a -4°C refrigerator overnight.
Centrifuge the precipitant at 15,000 rpm at 4°C to obtain dark brown precipitate.
Filter out the precipitate and wash it with ethanol two to three times.
Re-dissolve the washed precipitate in 2 mL chloroform.
Mix 500 μL of gold nanocluster solution (3.64×10-5 mol Au) with 10 mL CTAB solution (6.86×10-2 g CTAB) to achieve a molar ratio of Au:CTAB = 1:5.
Stir the mixture vigorously until no phase boundary is observed.
Leave the solution in a 55°C water bath for 3 hours to evaporate chloroform and obtain an aqueous solution of gold nanoclusters.
Make a 3.64×10-2 mol/L aqueous solution of gold nanocluster, which should be light brown.
Store the final aqueous gold nanocluster solution at 4°C in darkness.
After lyophilization, store the sample at 4°C for long-term preservation.
Prepare pH 5.0 acetic acid/sodium acetate buffer.
Make a 4 mL 0.5 mg/mL chitosan solution with the buffer by sonication for 30 minutes at room temperature.
Dissolve 0.8 mg RGO in 1.5 mL of the chitosan solution through sonication for about 1 hour until there is no black precipitate.
Add the aqueous RGO solution to the GNCs (3.64×10^-5 mol) at a 10:1 molar ratio of RGO/GNCs and homogenize in an ultrasonic bath for 30 minutes.
Incubate the reaction mixture in the dark for 1 hour to allow loading of the GNCs onto RGO.
Centrifuge the final mixture at 15000 rpm for 10 minutes to separate it.
Remove the supernatant and wash the aggregates with Millipore water twice to remove residual RGO.
Store the sample at 4℃ after lyophilization.
Prepare a 1 μg/mL aqueous solution of GNC-RGO nanocomposites.
Incubate the nanocomposites with a 0.22 μg/mL Doxorubicin (DOX) solution for 1 hour at 37℃ in a water bath.
Separate drug-loaded GNC-RGO samples through centrifugation at 10000 rpm for 15 minutes.
Wash the separated samples carefully three times with ultrapure water.
Seed 500,000 HepG2 cells in a 35 mm petri dish with a glass bottom overnight.
Load 0.25 μg/mL DOX or DOX-loaded GNC-RGO nanocomposites and incubate with the cells for 24 hours.
Wash the cells twice with PBS.
Load fresh medium into the petri dish.
Acquire images on a confocal fluorescent microscope using a 490 nm excitation laser beam and a 40 X objective lens.
